name: nearest-parents
description:
The parent from a list with the most words for each phrase, or an empty cell when it has none.

parents: the phrases that may be parents; a parent is a phrase whose words all stand in the phrase.

Between parents with as many words, the one whose words stand later in the phrase wins («a b c»: «b c» before «a c»), then the first in the list. Empty items of the list are skipped.

The step writes its result to a new column <column>_parent.

Example: semkit read core.csv nearest-parents 'диван,купить диван' write out.csv

options.name: --parents
options.description: the phrases that may be parents; a parent is a phrase whose words all stand in the phrase. Items: a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table) or @NAME of a list.

options.name: --as
options.description: Write the result to a new column NAME and keep the working column as it is.

arguments.name: PARENTS
arguments.description: the phrases that may be parents; a parent is a phrase whose words all stand in the phrase. Items: a comma list 'a,b', @FILE (one item per line, or the first column of a table) or @NAME of a list. The same as --parents PARENTS.
